S1.name: Losing the sign of the starting number
S1.example: Rewriting −3 + 5 as 3 + 5. Keep the starting value −3; the answer is 2.

S2.name: Treating addition of a negative as addition of a positive

S3.name: Failing to reverse the change when subtracting a negative

S4.name: Applying “two minuses make a plus” to unrelated signs
S4.example: Rewriting −4 − 3 as 4 + 3. The starting sign and subtraction operation do not cancel; the result is −7.

S5.name: Choosing the wrong sign after calculating the difference of magnitudes
S5.example: Writing −7 + 3 = 4. The result remains below zero: −4.

S6.name: Number-line direction or counting error despite a correct symbolic operation
S6.example: Moving left for −2 + 5, or counting the starting tick as move one and stopping at 2. Move five intervals right to 3. These are separate candidate faults, not automatically two errors in one diagram.

S7.name: Starting a later operation from zero/original input instead of the intermediate result
S7.example: For −3 + 8 − 2, correctly reach 5, then restart the second arrow at 0. Continue from 5 to 3.
